value.rationale: Edge identification of two cliques is a natural two-vertex-separator graph operation, and the canonical Banach endpoint projection norms measure worst-case absolute current amplification across that interface. The result determines all five edge-orbit values, proves distinct cut/cycle optimizing-phase boundaries and establishes an infinite family where the complementary norms attain on opposite private sides. The sharp unattained constants three and four differ from the limiting separate-clique constants two and three. These address a precise structural effect of graph composition, rather than an arbitrary finite instance.
